claim: Amazon Inspector is an automated vulnerability management service that continually scans EC2 instances, Lambda functions and container images (in Amazon ECR and in CI/CD tools) for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure.
question: What does Amazon Inspector scan, and for what?

values.display: an automated vulnerability management service

evidence.quote: Amazon Inspector is an automated vulnerability management service that continually scans Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2), AWS Lambda functions, and container images in Amazon ECR and within continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) tools, in near-real time for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure.

claim: The current Amazon Inspector was rearchitected and rebuilt as a new vulnerability management service, replacing the design of Inspector Classic.
question: How does Amazon Inspector relate to Amazon Inspector Classic?

values.display: rearchitected and rebuilt

evidence.quote: Amazon Inspector has been rearchitected and rebuilt to create a new vulnerability management service. Here are the key enhancements over Amazon Inspector Classic:

claim: Amazon Inspector has no limit on the number of instances or images it can scan at a time.
question: Is there a limit on how many instances or images Amazon Inspector scans at a time?

values.display: no limit to the number of instances or images

evidence.quote: There’s no limit to the number of instances or images that can be scanned at a time.

claim: Unlike Inspector Classic, Amazon Inspector needs no standalone Inspector agent on EC2 instances; it uses the AWS Systems Manager Agent (SSM Agent).
question: Which agent does the current Amazon Inspector use on EC2 instead of the Inspector Classic agent?

values.display: AWS Systems Manager Agent (SSM Agent)

evidence.quote: The new Amazon Inspector uses the widely deployed AWS Systems Manager Agent (SSM Agent), which removes that need.

claim: Amazon Inspector and Amazon Inspector Classic can be used at the same time in the same account.
question: Can Amazon Inspector and Inspector Classic run in the same account at the same time?

values.display: you can use both simultaneously

evidence.quote: Yes, you can use both simultaneously in the same account.

claim: Inspector container image scanning (ECR enhanced scanning) finds vulnerabilities in OS packages and programming language packages; ECR basic scanning finds them only in OS packages.
question: Which packages does ECR enhanced scanning (Inspector) cover compared with ECR basic scanning?

values.display: Identifies software vulnerabilities only in OS packages

evidence.quote: | Package coverage | Identifies vulnerabilities in both operating system (OS) packages and programming language (such as Python, Java, and Ruby) packages | Identifies software vulnerabilities only in OS packages |
evidence.table_header: |  | Amazon Inspector container image scanning (ECR enhanced scanning) | Amazon ECR native container image scanning (ECR basic scanning) |

claim: ECR enhanced scanning (Inspector) offers continual and on-push scanning; ECR basic scanning offers only on-push scanning.
question: How often does ECR enhanced scanning scan compared with ECR basic scanning?

values.display: Offers only on-push scanning
both continual scanning and on-push scanning

evidence.quote: | Scanning frequency | Offers both continual scanning and on-push scanning | Offers only on-push scanning |
evidence.table_header: |  | Amazon Inspector container image scanning (ECR enhanced scanning) | Amazon ECR native container image scanning (ECR basic scanning) |

claim: ECR enhanced scanning (Inspector) integrates with Security Hub, Organizations and EventBridge; ECR basic scanning has no built-in integrations with other AWS services.
question: Which AWS service integrations does ECR enhanced scanning have that ECR basic scanning lacks?

values.display: No built-in integrations with other AWS services

evidence.quote: | AWS service integrations | Integrated with AWS Security Hub, AWS Organizations, and AWS EventBridge | No built-in integrations with other AWS services are available |
evidence.table_header: |  | Amazon Inspector container image scanning (ECR enhanced scanning) | Amazon ECR native container image scanning (ECR basic scanning) |

claim: Every account new to Amazon Inspector gets a 15-day free trial, during which eligible EC2 instances, Lambda functions and container images pushed to ECR are scanned continually at no cost.
question: How long is the Amazon Inspector free trial?

values.display: 15-day free trial

qualifiers.scope: per account new to Amazon Inspector

evidence.quote: All accounts new to Amazon Inspector are eligible for a 15-day free trial to evaluate the service and estimate its cost. During the trial, all eligible Amazon EC2 instances, AWS Lambda functions, and container images pushed to Amazon ECR are continually scanned at no cost.

claim: Amazon Inspector integrates with AWS Organizations: a delegated administrator account manages Inspector centrally and views and manages findings for all accounts in the organization.
question: How do you manage Amazon Inspector for a whole organization?

values.display: Amazon Inspector is integrated with AWS Organizations

evidence.quote: Amazon Inspector is integrated with AWS Organizations. You can assign a DA account for Amazon Inspector, which acts as the primary administrator account for Amazon Inspector and can manage and configure it centrally. The DA account can centrally view and manage findings for all the accounts that are part of your AWS organization.

claim: When you start Amazon Inspector for the first time, EC2 scanning, Lambda scanning and ECR container image scanning are all activated by default; you can deactivate any of them.
question: Which Amazon Inspector scan types are on by default for a new user?

values.display: activated by default

qualifiers.scope: new Amazon Inspector users, all accounts in the organization
qualifiers.condition: starting Amazon Inspector for the first time

evidence.quote: If you’re starting Amazon Inspector for the first time, all scanning types, including EC2 scanning, Lambda scanning, and ECR container image scanning are activated by default. However, you can deactivate any or all of these across all accounts in your organization.

claim: Amazon Inspector does not need an agent: for EC2 it can use the SSM Agent (agent-based) or agentless scanning when the SSM Agent is not deployed, and container image, Lambda and network reachability scans need no agents.
question: Do you need an agent to use Amazon Inspector?

values.display: you don’t need an agent for scanning
Amazon Inspector also offers agentless scanning

evidence.quote: No, you don’t need an agent for scanning. For vulnerability scanning of Amazon EC2 instances, you can use the AWS Systems Manager Agent (SSM Agent) for an agent-based solution. Amazon Inspector also offers agentless scanning if you don’t have the SSM Agent deployed or configured. For assessing network reachability of Amazon EC2 instances, vulnerability scanning of container images, or vulnerability scanning of Lambda functions, no agents are necessary.

note: d114; agentless EC2 scanning is a post-2022 addition (changes lens should date it)

claim: Amazon Inspector scans are event-based: every workload is scanned on discovery and rescanned later, for example when a new CVE is published.
question: How often does Amazon Inspector scan?

values.display: All scans are automatically performed based on events

evidence.quote: All scans are automatically performed based on events. All workloads are initially scanned upon discovery and subsequently rescanned.

claim: For EC2, SSM agent-based rescans start on package changes, new CVEs or package updates, while agentless scans run every 24 hours.
question: How often does Amazon Inspector run agentless EC2 scans?

values.display: every 24 hours

evidence.quote: For SSM agent-based scans, rescans are started when a new software package is installed or uninstalled on an instance, when a new CVE is published, and after a vulnerable package is updated (to confirm there are no additional vulnerabilities). For agentless scans, scans are performed every 24 hours.

claim: The rescan duration for ECR images by last-in-use date is 14 days by default and can be set to 30, 60, 90 or 180 days.
question: What is the default rescan duration for ECR container images in Amazon Inspector?

values.display: 14 days (by default)

qualifiers.scope: ECR images configured for continual scanning, image last in use date

evidence.quote: Available re-scan duration configurations for image last in use date are 14 days (by default), 30 days, 60 days, 90 days, or 180 days.

claim: You can exclude an EC2 instance from Amazon Inspector scanning by adding a resource tag with the key InspectorEc2Exclusion.
question: How do you exclude an EC2 instance from Amazon Inspector scanning?

values.display: excluded from scanning by adding a resource tag

evidence.quote: Yes, an EC2 instance can be excluded from scanning by adding a resource tag. You can use the key ‘InspectorEc2Exclusion’, and value is <optional>.

claim: The Amazon Inspector risk score is a contextual score for each finding that correlates CVE information with network reachability, exploitability data and social media trends.
question: What is the Amazon Inspector risk score based on?

values.display: a highly contextualized score

evidence.quote: The Amazon Inspector risk score is a highly contextualized score that is generated for each finding by correlating common vulnerabilities and exposures (CVE) information with network reachability results, exploitability data, and social media trends.

claim: For new Amazon Inspector customers, hybrid scan mode is on by default when EC2 scanning is enabled: Inspector uses SSM Agents and falls back to agentless scanning for instances without a working SSM Agent.
question: What EC2 scan mode does a new Amazon Inspector customer get by default?

values.display: hybrid scan mode is turned on by default

qualifiers.scope: new Amazon Inspector customers, EC2 scanning

evidence.quote: For new Amazon Inspector customers, hybrid scan mode is turned on by default when you enable EC2 scanning. In the hybrid scan mode, Amazon Inspector relies on SSM Agents for application inventory collection to perform vulnerability assessments and automatically falls back on agentless scanning for instances that don’t have SSM Agents installed or configured.

claim: Amazon Inspector sends events such as new findings to EventBridge, logs API calls with CloudTrail and sends findings to Security Hub.
question: Which AWS services does Amazon Inspector integrate with for notifications and logging?

values.display: Amazon Inspector integrates with Amazon EventBridge

evidence.quote: Amazon Inspector integrates with Amazon EventBridge to provide notification for events such as a new finding, change of state of a finding, or creation of a suppression rule. Amazon Inspector also integrates with AWS CloudTrail for call logging.

note: Security Hub part of the claim: the FAQ's third sentence lacks a final period; see inspector-faq-sends-findings-to-security-hub if added by another lens

claim: Amazon Inspector can run on-demand, targeted assessments of EC2 instances against OS-level CIS configuration benchmarks across an organization.
question: Can Amazon Inspector check EC2 instances against CIS operating system benchmarks?

values.display: OS-level CIS configuration benchmarks

evidence.quote: You can run Amazon Inspector to perform on-demand and targeted assessments against OS-level CIS configuration benchmarks for Amazon EC2 instances across your AWS Organization.

claim: Amazon Inspector does not support a suspended state.
question: Can you suspend Amazon Inspector?

values.display: Amazon Inspector does not support a suspended state

evidence.quote: Amazon Inspector does not support a suspended state.
